headline: Welcome to the live coverage of stage 8 of La Vuelta 26
subtext: After the first breakaway success of La Vuelta 26, claimed by Andreas Leknessund at Aramon Valdelinares, the sprinters eye a fresh opportunity to battle it out with just over 1,200 metres of elevation gain between Puçol and Xeraco (171 km). They will need to overcome the Puerto de Barx (cat. 3) as they enter the final 30 kilometres. The neutral start is set at 13:25, the start proper at 13:42 after an 8 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around 17:30.

headline: 2 new stage towns on the map La Vuelta
subtext: Puçol and Xeraco make their debut as La Vuelta stage town. The full list of new stage towns in this edition: Monaco (stage 1), Manosque (2), Font-Romeu (stage 3), Falset (5), Roquetes (5), Vall d’Alba (7), Puçol (8), Xeraco (8), La Vila Joiosa (9), Alcaraz (10), Elche de la Sierra (10), Vera (12), Almuñécar (13), Palma del Rio (15), Cortegana (16), La Rábida (16), Dos Hermanas (17), El Puerto de Santa María (18), La Calahorra (20), and Collado del Aguacil (20).

headline: On the roads of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana
subtext: Both Puçol and Xeraco have been stage towns for the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana, the main local cycling event in the area. The race was born as the Vuelta al Levante in 1929. The winner’s list was opened by local hero Salvador Cardona, crowned in Valencia a few weeks after he had became the first Spanish stage winner at the Tour de France. Remco Evenepoel won the 77th edition in February 2026. Raul Garcia Pierna won the final stage in Valencia. Three riders of La Vuelta 26 have won the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana: Tadej Pogacar (2020), Stefan Küng (2021), and Santiago Buitrago (2025). The Volta CV Feminas has been held as a one day race since 2019 and most recently crowned Movistar’s Liane Lippert.

headline: Pogacar’s 250th Grand Tour distinctive jersey
subtext: Tadej Pogacar received yesterday his 249th and 250th Grand Tour distinctive jerseys: - 97 as the overall leader (71 in the Tour, 6 in La Vuelta, 20 in the Giro) - 8 as the leader of points standings (3 in the Tour, 5 in La Vuelta) - 63 as the leader of the mountains standings (39 in the Tour, 4 in La Vuelta, 20 in the Giro) - 82 as the leader of the young riders standings (75 in the Tour, 7 in La Vuelta)

headline: First too cold, now too hot
Let’s roll
subtext: The peloton make their way to the start proper with an 8 km parade. There are 177 riders as Luca Van Boven (Lotto Intermarché) doesn't start after his crash yesterday.

headline: La Roja
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) slightly increased his GC lead with a late attack to Aramon Valdelinares. Enric Mas (Movistar) now trails by 3’50’’, and Primoz Roglic (Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) by 4’50’’. The gap to Felix Gall (Decathlon CMA CGM) is up to 5’01’’. Sepp Kuss (Visma-Lease a Bike) completes the top 5 with a gap of 6’05’’, just ahead of Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos), trailing by 6’06’’. Richard Carapaz (EF Education-EasyPost) dropped to the 7th place (+6’12’’).

headline: Green jersey
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) had been leading the points standings since his victory in Monaco, but Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) passed him with his long range assault yesterday: 104 points for the Belgian against 102 for the Slovenian. Van Aert already led the points standings for 13 days before crashing out of La Vuelta 24. His teammate Matthew Brennan is third with 60 points.

headline: Polka dot jersey
subtext: Tadej Pogacar (UAE Emirates XRG) still leads the mountains standings (29 points) but there’s a new chaser: Andreas Leknessund (Uno-X Mobility), who took 19 KOM points yesterday and will wear the polka dot jersey today. Enric Mas (Movistar) is third with 14 points.

headline: White jersey
subtext: Breakaway riders Jakob Omrzel (Bahrain Victorious) and Léo Bisiaux (Decathlon CMA CGM) made the most of yesterday’s breakaway to move up the ladder in the best young rider standings while Ramses Debruyne (Alpecin-Premier Tech) dropped from the second to the sixth place. Oscar Onley (Netcompany Ineos) still leads, with Omrzel in second (3’48’’) and Bisiaux in third (6’07’’).

headline: Team standings
subtext: With Léo Bisiaux (9th), Felix Gall (20th) and Gregor Mühlberger (25th), Decathlon CMA CGM had the best collective performance again. They now lead the team standings with a gap of 12’04’’ on UAE Emirates XRG and 20’35’’ on Visma-Lease a Bike.

headline: Combativity award
subtext: Wout van Aert (Visma-Lease a Bike) will once again race with a distinctive bib today as he was named the most combative rider yesterday.

headline: To see Fernandez in the breakaway comes as no surprise...
subtext: Already on the move on day 2, the Burgos-Burpellet-BH baroudeur had announced his ambition at the start: “I’ve been finding my rhythm out there in the breakaway on the second day. We’ll try to make our presence felt in the breakaway on more days. I’m happy with how things are going. It’s a stage that could clearly come down to a sprint, and hopefully, in the end, getting into the breakaway will be easier than it has been over the last few days; and we’ll have to be in it, of course, to show our team. That’s the plan for today. Of course, [our sprinter] César Macias is very motivated. It’s his first Vuelta. He’s been having a great time so far. I think he’s in excellent form. He’ll try to enjoy the finish.”

headline: Fernandez is in Betera
subtext: Several stages of the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana and the last two editions of the the Volta CV Feminas started in Betera (km 32.8). It was notably the case in 2026. Raul Garcia Pierna won the final stage of the men’s event while Remco Evenepoel sealed the overall victory; Liane Lippert won the women’s event. Betera is also the hometown of Francisco Navarro, the winner of stage 5 of La Vuelta 1988.

headline: Fernandez in his favourite role
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) was already part of the breakaway on the second stage, on the way to Manosque. He’s Burgos Burpellet BH’s breakaway specialist. This year, he’s attacked in two stages of O Gran Camiño, one in Itzulia and one in the GP Miguel Indurain. Last year, when he made his La Vuelta debut before having to abandon on stage 12 due to the illness that affected the team, he was also part of the breakaway on stage 2 en route to Limone Piemonte and rode solo for a few kilometres on stage 4 en route to Voiron. “We’ll have Sinuhé Fernández as a team-mate and a very combative climber for all kinds of stages,” said DS Damien Garcia in the team’s press release ahead of La Vuelta 26.

headline: Splits in the bunch
subtext: The pace has increased, and the gap has decreased (5'10'').

headline: Winning streaks - Uno-X Mobility leads the way alongside UAE Emirates XRG and Visma-Lease a Bike
subtext: The three teams with stage wins at La Vuelta so far - UAE Emirates XRG, Visma-Lease a Bike and Uno-X Mobility - also won in the Giro d’Italia and in the Tour de France. The Norwegian team have won a stage in each of the last four Grand Tours they’ve participated in (Tour 2025, Giro 2026, Tour 2026, La Vuelta 26). For UAE Emirates XRG, the streak has been going since Tadej Pogacar’s victories at La Vuelta 19 (22 consecutive Grand Tours with a stage win). Visma-Lease a Bike have won stages in every Grand Tour since the Tour 2021 (17 Grand Tours).Lidl-Trek, Soudal Quick-Step and EF Education-EasyPost are in a position to take wins in this year’s three Grand Tours. Groupama-FDJ United, Lotto Intermarché, Movistar, NSN and Picnic PostNL are the five UCI WorldTeams with no Grand Tour stage win so far this year.

headline: Elosegui: "It brings back some very fond memories for our family"
subtext: Íñigo Elosegui (Kern Pharma) had great stories to tell this morning at the start: “Yes, my grandfather [José Antonio Momeñe] won in Valencia in 1966. And on top of that, he took the lead in La Vuelta! It brings back some very fond memories for our family. I’ve also won a few races here in the Valencian Community, so it’s a place that brings back fond memories for us. I’ve always wanted to follow in my grandfather’s footsteps, but he was simply too good. Here, we’re taking it one day at a time. We want to win a stage – and why not? There’s a good finish for the sprinters; we’ve got a good sprinter in the team [Marc Brustenga] and my job is to try and help him contest the finish.”

headline: One Sinuhé amongst 121
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is one of 121 Spanish citizens named Sinuhé, according to the Spanish National Institute of Statistics. “It’s an unusual name that my father gave me because of a book. The book is called Sinuhé the Egyptian. He read it, liked the name, thought it was original, and gave it to me for that reason,” he explained to us last year.

subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) is 104 km from the finish, and the peloton are 4'05'' behind him.

headline: Tanti auguri Jacopo Mosca
subtext: Lidl-Trek's Italian rider turns 33 years old today. At the start, he spoke about his life on the roads with his partner Elisa Longo Borghini: "My wife is at home training. She was here in Monaco, so now she’s back to work. We are two totally different roles in cycling, but still we both ride the bike, so in the end it’s no so difficult. We have to train, spend the life together when we can and make a lot of Tetris to try to see each other. But, apparently, more and more people are doing this in cycling! We can see a lot of couples. It’s hard, but it’s always nice."

subtext: Guillaume Martin-Guyonnet (Groupama-FDJ United) is on his wheel.

headline: Marti: "The best place in the world"
subtext: Hailing from Moixent, around 50 kilometres west of the Puerto de Barx, Pau Marti (NSN) is the local rider of the day. He was delighted at the start: “We’re in Valencia and I think this is the best place in the world: great weather, good roads, and I’m sure there’ll be a brilliant atmosphere on today’s stage. It’ll be a flat route to start with, but certainly very fast, and then there’s the Puerto de Barx, which doesn’t have particularly steep gradients, but it’s bound to be a key point in the race where some teams will try to drop the fast riders, and then the stretch to the finish will be very fast too, through Xeraco and along the beach – which is also absolutely lovely.”

headline: The average speed after 2 hours: 41.9 km/h
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos-Burpellet-BH) is 75 km from the finish. The peloton trail by 2'25''.

headline: Dversnes: "Cort will be our best shot"
subtext: Sinuhé Fernandez (Burgos Burpellet BH) could use some advice from Fredrik Dversnes (Uno-X Mobility), who managed to upset the sprinters in the Giro this year: “It’s about having some bad days to lower other's expectations, then come in a breakaway with rather smaller guys that have much bigger engines than you think, and then you just hammer away and win. As you see I've put on my fast gear today, single speed on the bike, high wheels and everything, so we are ready for it! But we think there will be a bunch sprint, so Magnus Cort will be our best shot there."

headline: Whatever it takes to cool down
The gap decreases again: 1'40''

headline: Brennan: "We have a plan"
subtext: Does Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) have to tell Wout van Aert what he needs to win the stage? “Not really, I think together we work really well. I think he really helps to show myself a little bit more and puts me in the right place, so it works well. I think we have a plan, and if we can execute that plan, we can complement both ambitions today. And yeah, I think today the main goal is to obviously go for the stage, and there’s still two weeks to go. So there’s a lot of opportunities to fight for the green jersey and increase the lead on Pogi, so we’ll just see what happens.”

headline: 1 minute

headline: Groves: "I’ve had some success in La Vuelta before, so we’ll try again today"
subtext: Alpecin-Premier Tech are well positioned at the front of the peloton. Kaden Groves has often met success on the seaside at La Vuelta... "I haven’t really looked much into the map, actually", the Australian sprinter said at the start. "But of course, I’ve had some success in La Vuelta before, so we’ll try again today. There’s still a strong sprint field here and we have to see. Of course, I think we can expect the normal guys to be in the front again today. I’ve had a tough start already of La Vuelta, so hopefully the legs are going to improve and I can have a good feeling. Today it’s a stage that suits me, of course we need to assess where I am at the top of the climb. Hopefully, with enough boys around me, I can come back. As far as the last part of the stage, it’s relatively straightforward, so I expect a normal big bunch sprint today. The wind shouldn’t play too much of a part, so I think it should be the first pure sprint stage of this Vuelta, at there’s not many of them!"

headline: Headed for the intermediate sprint and the Puerto de Barx
subtext: Puerto de Barx is an emblematic ascent in the area, very often featured in the Volta a la Comunitat Valenciana. Both in 2025 and 2026, it has been the perfect launchpad for Demi Vollering to take her first victory of the season in Gandia, right next to Xeraco.
